candidates.prompt_text: Do you want to join a school club? Please say what club you would choose and why.
suggested_ideas: what people do in the club
why it is interesting to you

evaluation_guide.expected_content: The student gives a simple personal answer about joining a school club, names a club, and gives one or more clear reasons.
evaluation_guide.key_points: A suitable club is named; the answer stays on the topic of school clubs; at least one reason is given, such as enjoyment, learning skills, meeting friends, or relaxing after class.
evaluation_guide.acceptable_responses: Any clear answer is acceptable, including wanting to join a sports club, music club, art club, reading club, science club, English club, volunteer club, or not wanting to join any club if the student explains why.
evaluation_guide.off_topic_examples: Talking only about regular school subjects, describing a family member, discussing travel plans, or giving a general opinion about school without mentioning a club.
evaluation_guide.scoring_hints: For fluency, reward smooth delivery, ability to continue speaking without long pauses, and simple self-correction that does not interrupt communication. Content can be basic if it is clear and sustained.
evaluation_guide.common_mistakes: Very short one-sentence answers; long unnatural pauses; repeating the same words many times; forgetting to name a club; giving reasons that are unclear or unrelated to the club.

candidates.prompt_text: Tell me about a school club that you think is useful for students.

evaluation_guide.expected_content: The student describes one school club and explains in a simple way why it is useful for students.
evaluation_guide.key_points: The club is identified; the student mentions some activities; the usefulness is explained with basic ideas such as learning, health, teamwork, confidence, or enjoyment.
evaluation_guide.acceptable_responses: Any school club is acceptable as long as the answer explains why it is useful. The student may speak about a real club at school or a common type of school club in general.
evaluation_guide.off_topic_examples: Explaining a favorite teacher, talking about a weekend hobby with no link to a school club, or discussing problems in education without describing a club.
evaluation_guide.scoring_hints: Focus on whether the speaker can keep talking at a steady pace with connected simple ideas. Minor grammar or word-choice problems are acceptable if the message remains easy to follow.
evaluation_guide.common_mistakes: Listing club names without explanation; giving memorized phrases with little meaning; stopping after a few words; losing the topic and speaking only about school life in general.

candidates.prompt_text: Which do you prefer: a sports club or an art club at school? Please explain your choice.

evaluation_guide.expected_content: The student chooses one of the two club types and gives simple reasons for the preference.
evaluation_guide.key_points: A clear choice is made; the answer includes at least one comparison or reason; the student mentions activities or personal interest related to the chosen club.
evaluation_guide.acceptable_responses: Either choice is acceptable. The student may also say both are good but one is better for them, as long as they clearly explain the preference.
evaluation_guide.off_topic_examples: Talking only about sports in general, only about drawing at home with no school club context, or discussing school rules without making a choice.
evaluation_guide.scoring_hints: Reward the ability to answer directly, continue speaking with little hesitation, and link reasons in a natural sequence. The comparison can be very simple because the task is low cognitive demand.
evaluation_guide.common_mistakes: Not making a clear choice; repeating the prompt without adding ideas; giving unrelated details; pausing too often while searching for basic words.
